solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Later perhaps, but not too late

definitions.meaning: eventually, after a while has passed, at some future point
punctually, before the deadline has passed

explanation.surface: Someone hedges about when they will arrive: later, maybe, but not too late.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both eventually and early enough, two senses of the same idiom.

clue.text: She brings peace to Greece

parts.note: the Greek goddess of peace, whose name comes from the Greek word for peace

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess personifying peace bore this name, also a woman's first name.

clue.text: Servant trouble makes these establishments harder to run nowadays

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of servant are stirred into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Problems with staff make inns hard to run these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges SERVANT. The definition plays on pubs closing, hard to run profitably today.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns and pubs are businesses whose running is harder now, with many closing.

clue.text: Form of variety before the 50s, much as I recollect

indicators.note: before places the anagram ahead of the numerals
recollect read as re-collect: the letters are gathered again into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: Someone remembers variety shows from before the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' is read as re-collect, gathering the letters afresh; 'before' sets the scrambled part ahead of the numerals. Music hall was British popular variety theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre, the popular stage entertainment of song, comedy and acts, took this name in Britain.

clue.text: Craft project

definitions.meaning: a large motorboat, a type of vessel
to send off or set going, as with a rocket or a new product

explanation.surface: A two-word note on an arts-and-crafts scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat of that name is a craft, and to set a project going is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: This may cause nearly everybody to take up weapons

indicators.note: nearly says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: everybody is all
to arm is to take up weapons

explanation.surface: A threat may provoke almost everyone to take up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL. The word comes from Italian all'arme, 'to arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear or a warning signal is what would cause people to rush to take up arms.

clue.text: A river once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the word goes upward, read backwards

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A river rises again and then falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns AGAIN into NIAGA. Niagara Falls is on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the Canada-US border are known by this single name.

clue.text: The man to approach for capital investment

parts.note: he is the man
to address someone is to approach or speak to them

explanation.surface: Go to the man in charge for capital funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means head, and something worn on the head is what one invests the head with.

clue.text: Man in a whirl — engine fuel his trouble?

parts.note: DERV is British slang for diesel fuel for road vehicles

indicators.note: trouble suggests the word his is disturbed and its letters stirred up

explanation.surface: A mechanic wonders whether diesel is what is making an engine spin wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns HIS into ISH. DERV (diesel engine road vehicle) is a British term for diesel.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish is a Sufi ascetic who spins in ecstatic dance, so a man in a whirl.

clue.text: Adam upset, bolted out fast

indicators.note: the verb sits out round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to bolt is to run off, so bolted is ran

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means overturned, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Adam is upset and storms off to go without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the name and 'out' puts the verb round it. 'Adam' wants to be the first man in a religious surface, which helps disguise the Muslim fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month is a period of daytime fasting, so the noun fast fits it.

clue.text: Rescuing army?

parts.note: the word for rescuing, which is also the first half of a Christian charity's name

explanation.definitionFit: Rescue from harm or sin is this word, and the Salvation Army is the Christian charity.

clue.text: Pipe bursts each summer

indicators.note: bursts suggests the words break apart and their letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A water pipe splits every summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' rearranges EACH SUMMER into the tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe with a bowl carved from a soft white clay mineral is named after that mineral.

clue.text: General assistant

parts.note: reads as a general dogsbody, but means an officer who assists a general

explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is the helper of a senior military officer such as a general.

clue.text: A seat arranged on board

indicators.note: arranged tells us the letters of a seat are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A seat has been booked for someone on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on the ocean is being aboard a ship, a common idiom.

clue.text: Completely irresponsible profligate

explanation.surface: A spendthrift is utterly reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means without restraint and also dissolute or immoral, two adjective senses.

clue.text: Set back after an instrument breaks

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the instrument

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: set back says the word set is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A musical instrument breaks and causes a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word, and 'after' places it behind the instrument. 'Set back' looks like one phrasal verb meaning delayed, but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a rule or law is to infringe it, the same transitive verb sense.

clue.text: Sort of stall for the frisky carthorse

indicators.note: a frisky horse is lively and skittish, so the letters of carthorse leap about

explanation.surface: A horse box suits a lively carthorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisky' rearranges CARTHORSE. Orchestra stalls are the theatre seats near the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalls in a theatre are the ground-floor seats, and the front ones are named after the players' pit.

clue.text: Don't drop round — it will produce no response

definitions.text: Don't drop round — it will produce no response

parts.words: Don't drop round — it will produce no response
parts.note: dropping round a home produces no reply; the phrase also means a joke or plan getting no reaction

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an attempt that fails to win any reaction, like a joke that gets no laughs.

clue.text: The French cry "Attack!"

parts.note: la is the French for the
a cry is a shout

explanation.surface: A Frenchman cries 'Attack!'
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out at someone violently is to attack them, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Angry indication that the answer isn't right

definitions.text: indication that the answer isn't right
definitions.meaning: the X mark a teacher puts beside a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher gets annoyed and marks a pupil's answer wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means annoyed, and is also the X-shaped mark used to show an error.

clue.text: Cover work that includes Ravel composition

indicators.note: includes says the work encloses the rearranged name

parts.note: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: composition means the letters of ravel are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cover version of a work includes a piece by Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges RAVEL into VERLA; OP 'includes' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend over part of something is to cover it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Side turning Caesar was warned about

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of side are twisted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Caesar was warned about an attack from the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges SIDE. Julius Caesar was warned by a soothsayer to beware the 15th of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The soothsayer's warning to Julius Caesar named this mid-March date, on which he was murdered.

clue.text: Rock group that's been around for a long time

definitions.text: Rock group that's been around for a long time

parts.words: Rock group that's been around for a long time
parts.note: suggests a veteran rock band, but means a ring of standing stones that has stood for millennia

explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric monument in Wiltshire is a circle of huge stones thousands of years old.

clue.text: I leave the elder Spaniard

indicators.note: I leave says the letter I departs from the word

parts.note: the elder of two is the senior

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave of an elderly Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from SENIOR to get the Spanish word for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for a man, equivalent to Mr or sir, stands for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Sudden blow to add nothing to one's enjoyment

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blow of wind
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sudden gust of wind adds nothing to someone's pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish or zest in doing something is keen enjoyment.

clue.text: Returning antelope occupied by kill gets coup de grace

indicators.note: occupied by says the reversed animal has the other piece living inside it
returning means the word for the antelope is read backwards

parts.note: the gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest
to do in is to kill

explanation.surface: A returning antelope is killed with a final blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses the animal and 'occupied by' puts the two-word kill inside it. A coup de grace is a finishing blow, hence one's ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de grace is the final blow that brings about someone's ruin or downfall.

clue.text: Uncertain how incompetent companies can operate

definitions.meaning: puzzled, not knowing what to do

explanation.surface: Badly run firms don't know what to do and end up trading in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bewildered, and literally a business trading unprofitably runs that way.

clue.text: Spot a doctor going back to the old

definitions.note: the clue reads this as one old person, a noun

parts.note: a spot is a dot

indicators.note: going back says the abbreviation is written in reverse

explanation.surface: A doctor spots an elderly patient on a return visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A senile old person is called by this word, someone weak-minded with age.

clue.text: Female poet delivers a couple of pages in curtailed performance

indicators.note: a performance delivering something brings it out from within, so the new letters sit inside
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a show is a performance
P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages is PP

explanation.surface: A woman poet reads a couple of pages at a cut-short recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last letter of the performance word, and 'delivers' puts the article and the pages inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek lyric poet of Lesbos was a woman, the most famous female poet of antiquity.
